text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, which saves time for everyone who works with it. One key habit is following naming conventions: use clear, meaningful names for variables and functions so their purpose is obvious. Another good practice is keeping functions small and focused on a single task. This makes the code simpler to test and reuse. Clean code is also easier to maintain, because fixing bugs or adding new features takes less effort. In short, readable code with good names and simple functions helps teams work faster and reduces mistakes.
